description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of various relational categories within the MMRA benchmark, which is designed to evaluate multi-granularity and multi-image relational association capabilities in large visual language models. The chart is composed of ten distinct slices, each representing a different relational category with its corresponding count and percentage of the total. The largest segment is "ObservationAngle," accounting for 126 instances (12.28%), followed by "SimilarMaterial" with 106 instances (10.33%). The "SubEvent" and "UsageSimilarity" categories each have 100 instances (9.74% and 9.65%, respectively). Several categories—“MentalitySimilarity,” “SimilarEvent,” “AppearanceSimilarity,” and “Layout”—each contain 90 instances (8.77%). The "RelativePosition" category has 81 instances (7.90%), "NearSameEntity" has 63 instances (6.34%), and the "SubEvent" category is shown with 100 instances (9.74%). The slices are arranged in a circular format, with each category labeled with its name, count, and percentage. The colors of the slices vary, including shades of teal, orange, red, brown, green, yellow, light blue, gray, dark gray, and light green, aiding in visual differentiation. The chart does not include a legend, but the labels are directly placed on or near each slice, making it easy to identify each category. The segments are not exploded or highlighted, maintaining a standard pie chart appearance. The percentages are displayed inside each slice, providing a clear visual representation of the proportion of each category within the benchmark.
